title: Glowing person (emissive body, fresnel rim, outline, halo shells)
summary: Makes any recon figure glow orange like the shot-match references: emissive body with a brighter yellow fresnel rim, skinned outline, additive halo shells for sunlit scenes. 3 tuned looks.

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

usage.import: import { glowPerson, glow, glowLight, glowCap } from '../library/module.recon.glow-person/index.js';

doc.when: Stylised 'glowing people' (heat-map / x-ray / ghost figures) in any recon shot: night interiors (cafe), moonlit exteriors (night), daylight (sunlit: halo shells, because bloom cannot isolate figures when the lit ground is brighter).
doc.avoid: Normal dressed characters (use figure() roles). Don't use bloom alone for glow in sunlit scenes.
gotchas: Set project settings.post.cap >= .95 (and ca 0): the Investigation grade caps highlights at .775 and turns hot orange pastel/peach.
Colours in LOOKS are LINEAR. Convert reference samples (sRGB) with fromRef() from module.recon.canvas-materials.
Every patched material sets customProgramCacheKey: three.js caches onBeforeCompile programs by function source, so shells that differ only in a number would share one program.
glow() on a bare figure hides every mesh except the largest skinned one (layer 31): face layers, hair, eyes.
glowCap must be added AFTER the tick that poses the figure (it follows the posed head).
In sunlit scenes keep roughness 1 and envMapIntensity 0 (the sun's white specular washed the figures peach).

params.looks: cafe | night | sunlit, or { body, outline, halos, haloColor }
